title: fix(post): never write an arc block whose written ends coincide
body:
## Cause

Two places turned a short arc into a full circle.

1. The posts. The arc path of each post wrote the end point of an arc record through its own word format (Fanuc inch: four decimals, a 2.54 um step). No post compared the written end with the written start. A short arc under the output step got the same X and Y words as its start and a nonzero I/J. A control reads that block as a full circle. The reporter (thank you, @qsmits, for the clear reproduction `tiny.cnc`) found it with two 1 um arcs (sweep about 0.007 degrees) on the Fanuc inch post. Metric also collides: two ends less than 1 um apart write the same three-decimal word.
2. The stream writer (found by the re-read). The app posts through `cnc::serialize`, which writes each position as whole micrometres. A generator arc with a chord under 1 um (#3463: a fillet can reach 0.09 um) rounded to a record whose end equals its start. The stream reader takes that form as a full turn (`full_circle_raw`), so every post wrote a full circle. Before this PR, the new app test posted `G02 X10.346 Y-2.98 Z2.5 I0. J-50. F800` for a 0.09 um fillet: a full circle of R50 through the part.

## The law

No post writes an arc block whose end point, as written (output unit, precision, work origin and modal words applied), equals its start point in the arc plane, unless the record is a full turn that the dialect writes as one block. The comparison uses the text of the words, not the stream's millimetres. The stream writer never writes a short arc in the stream's full-turn form.

## The change

- The posts: one rule in one place, `arcFate(word)` / `arcFateOf(shape, word)` in the PRELUDE (`crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs`, appended by `Script::load`). Each script calls it with its own word function.
  - `"arc"`: the written in-plane ends differ, or the record turns more than half a circle (its sweep from its direction and centre), or its ends are equal in the stream (the stated full turn), or it states no finite centre (the script's own refusal by name runs). The arc posts as before. No distance band: a true short arc with a tiny chord is still short.
  - `"linear"`: a short arc whose ends coincide as written, while Z (a helix) or a rotary still moves. The post writes its own straight feed move (`onLinear`) to the end point.
  - `"none"`: a short arc whose ends coincide, and nothing changes as written. No motion block. The feed and the modal state are not touched.
- The stream writer: `crates/post/src/post/cnc_arc_lattice.rs`, called by `cnc::serialize` (the one place that the whole-job, per-operation and per-mount paths use: `posting.rs`, `posting_per_op.rs`, `posting_mounts.rs`). The writer tracks the true start of each arc. An arc whose in-plane ends round to the same micrometre and whose true sweep is half a turn or less is written as a `Feed` to its rounded end. A near-full turn and a stated full turn keep their arc record. The record stays, also when nothing moves (a zero-length `Feed`), because the viewer map counts stream records as toolpath moves.
- The stream reader is not made stricter: equal ends stay the stated full-turn form (`full_circle_raw`, with a golden on every post). With the writer fixed, our own streams never use that form for a short arc. The decision file says why a refusal and a zero-sweep reading were dropped.
- The R-word mode (`useRadiusArcs`) comes after the guard. A short arc that the output can show keeps its minor (positive R) solution.
- Klartext no longer refuses the short case. Its refusal stays only for a near-full turn with coincident written ends.
- `heidenhain.cps` `verticalArc`: a record with equal ends in G18/G19 is a full circle of chords. Before, it was one zero-length chord.
- No input refusal: an arc of 0.007 degrees stays legal input.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3442-coincident-arc-blocks.md` (chosen, why, dropped).

## The reporter's file, Fanuc, `--units inch`

Before (each block is a full circle on the control):

```
G03 X0.7135 Y0.2139 Z0.2165 I-0.315 J0. F7.09
G03 X0.7135 Y0.2139 Z0.2165 I-0.315 J0. F7.09
```

After: no arc block. The plunge ends at `X0.7135 Y0.2139`, and the next motion block is the rapid retract. The two arcs move the tool less than 0.0001 in, so the tool is never further from the programmed path than the output step.

## Every shipped post

| Post | Guard site | Guarded | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| carvera | `onCircular` (mm only) | yes | table (b) |
| doosan-dnm | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | table (b), R mode, rotary |
| fanuc | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | (a), (b), (c), R mode, rotary, app tests |
| fanuc-lathe | `meridianArc`, on its X (diameter) and Z words | yes | table (b), lathe witness |
| grbl | `onCircular` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| grblhal | `onCircular` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| haas | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| heidenhain (DIN/ISO) | `onCircular`, after the cycle refusal (mm only) | yes | table (b) |
| heidenhain-klartext | `onCircular`, on its rounded preset values (mm only) | yes | table (b), near-full refusal |
| linuxcnc | `onCircular` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| mach4 | `onCircular`, on the machine-frame words after the trunnion transform | yes | table (b) |
| mazak | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| sinker-iso | refuses every arc (no change) | yes | table (b): no arc block |
| sinumerik | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | table (b) |
| sodick-wire | `onCircular`, after `cutOk` | yes | table (b), flat witness |
| tinyg | `onCircular` (its by-name refusal of the short case is replaced) | yes | table (b), app `tinyg_post` |
| tormach | `onCircular` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| tormach-lathe | `meridianArc` | yes | table (b), lathe witness |
| tormach-plasma | `onCircular`, after the compensation refusal | yes | table (b), flat witness |
| wire-iso | `onCircular`, after the taper refusal | yes | table (b), flat witness |

Every post is also behind the stream writer rule for programs that the app posts.

## Tests (red first, green on this head)

`crates/post/tests/coincident_arcs.rs` (reader in `coincident_arcs/reader.rs`, the reporter's input in `coincident_arcs/tiny.cnc`): `test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed`.
- (a) `fanuc_inch_writes_no_full_circle_for_the_reporters_short_arcs`
- (b) `every_post_writes_no_coincident_arc_block_and_keeps_its_real_arcs`: all 20 posts, mm and inch where the post writes inch, and the R mode where the script has it. Witness: two sub-resolution XY arcs (0.03 um and 0.01 um, so the second is under 10 nm), one sub-resolution helical arc, one normal quarter arc, one full circle as two halves, one sub-resolution G18 arc (lathes: a meridian arc; plasma and wire: the flat part). The law holds, and the output is byte-identical to a reference stream that has the short arcs as what they must post as.
- (c) `fanuc_mm_three_decimal_collision_is_no_arc_block`
- `a_short_resolvable_r_arc_keeps_its_minor_solution`
- `arc_fate_reads_the_written_words_and_leaves_a_centreless_arc_to_its_script`: the rule's answers (short, near-full, helix, rotary, 1e-6 mm ahead is a short helix, 1e-6 mm behind is a full turn, equal ends, sub-step radius, G18 both directions, no centre).
- `a_full_helical_turn_off_by_float_noise_stays_a_helix`: every mill post, mm and inch.
- `a_near_full_turn_with_coincident_written_ends_posts_one_full_circle`: every mill post, mm and inch (Fanuc: one `G03` with I/J; Klartext refuses by name; TinyG writes two halves).
- `a_short_arc_with_a_rotary_word_posts_the_rotary_move`: Fanuc and Doosan on the tilt-head machine, mm and inch: `G01` with `A1.`. (Haas refuses a tilted move without RTCP by name, so it cannot run this case.)

`crates/post/tests/cnc_arc_lattice.rs` (the writer): `test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed`.
- `a_short_arc_under_one_micrometre_is_written_as_a_feed` (XY, helix, G18)
- `a_near_full_turn_a_stated_full_turn_and_a_visible_arc_keep_their_arc_record`

`crates/app/tests/short_arc_lattice.rs` (the real app paths, a 0.09 um R50 fillet spliced into a generated contour, Fanuc, mm and inch): `test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed`.
- `a_sub_micrometre_fillet_posts_no_full_circle_through_the_whole_job_path`
- `a_sub_micrometre_fillet_posts_no_full_circle_per_operation_and_per_mount`
- Red without the writer change: both FAILED, `inch=false: full circles ["G02 X10.346 Y-2.98 Z2.5 I0. J-50. F800"]`.

Red on the earlier heads: on main, (a), (b) and (c) failed (every post wrote coincident blocks, Klartext refused, tinyg refused). On 8bae4e111, the rule test and the noisy helix failed. On 40e1baae7, both app tests failed (above).

True full circles from generators: the bore and circular goldens are unchanged (`golden_cl`, `conformance`, `bore_cycle`, the recorded `full_circle` / `full_circle_raw` suites of every post are green). No golden file changed in this PR.

Changed tests, each because it pinned the fault:
- `radius_arcs.rs` `major_arcs_use_negative_r_and_degenerate_arcs_fall_back_to_ijk`: the `tiny_inch` case wrote an I/J block with its ends and its centre at `X0. Y0.`. It now expects no arc block and no warning.
- app `tinyg_post.rs` `rounded_coincident_xy_arc_endpoints_are_refused` is now `rounded_coincident_xy_arc_endpoints_post_no_arc_block`. The test count is the same.

## Gate (head 532d0fa92)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run`: 251 steps (the diff under `assets/posts/` maps to many app suites). By the brief, I ran these instead:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post -j 6 --no-fail-fast`: 117 test binaries, 0 failed.
  - app binaries `short_arc_lattice`, `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `posting`, `bore_cycle`, `between_setups`, `control_comp`, `carvera_post`, `grblhal_post`, `klartext_builtin`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_inch`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `linuxcnc_post`, `mach4_builtin`, `microarc_test_part`, `plasma_post`, `post_unit_word`, `sodick_wire_post`, `tinyg_post`, `tormach_post`, `wire_post`: 22 binaries, all ok.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test short_arc_lattice -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main`, 207 steps): not run yet. The run waits for the heavy-run lock. The PR stays a draft until the lanes ran.

## Not exercised

No control or machine ran the output. The full-circle reading of a coincident block is from the public programming manuals, not from a control. The other app suites of the quick plan were not run in debug.

## Follow-up

#3463: the generators can emit arcs with a chord under 1 um (fillets, fitted pieces, entry arcs). After this PR, the app's stream writes such an arc as a straight move and every post refuses to write a coincident arc block, so the posted program does not cut a full circle. The toolpath, the simulation and the CL file still carry the sub-micrometre arc: this PR does not change the generators, and #3463 stays open.

Changelog: Posts never write an arc block whose written end point is its start point (a control reads it as a full circle): an arc shorter than the output step, or shorter than the stream's micrometre step, now posts as a straight move (helix) or as no block, in every shipped post and unit.

Effort: high

Refs #3463

Fixes #3442
